title: Reference systems are pattern mines, not blueprints
statement: Reverse engineer an external system by problem/capability, extract transferable patterns and complexity, then run a gap analysis before architecture decisions.
applicability: Any product team studying external systems as references.

title: One entity, one identity, multiple views
statement: CRM, prospecting, map, agenda, reports and AI should operate on canonical entities rather than maintain parallel copies.
applicability: Systems with multiple modules/views over the same business entities.

title: AI over structured truth
statement: AI should consume selective structured context and propose actions; important writes pass through controlled domain operations and review rather than treating AI as the database.
applicability: AI-enabled operational systems with persistent business data.

title: Strangler migration with reversible vertical slices
statement: Replace legacy behavior incrementally with adapters, reconciliation, feature flags and rollback windows instead of a big-bang rewrite.
applicability: Brownfield migrations where continuity and rollback matter.

title: Professional gates may block release
statement: Environment or test limitations should block/label a release rather than be hidden or reported as success.
applicability: Release processes where environment/test uncertainty can hide risk.

title: Foundation plus visible user value
statement: Whenever safe, infrastructure packages should unlock a perceptible workflow improvement; UX polish should evolve with domain migration rather than as an isolated redesign.
applicability: Product migrations where infrastructure work must preserve user momentum.

title: Proportional ceremony by risk
statement: Use MICRO, STANDARD and STRUCTURAL paths so low-risk work stays fast while structural work receives evidence/architecture/safety discipline.
applicability: Any engineering/product workflow where one process risks becoming bureaucratic.

title: Machine store + generated human index
statement: Keep JSONL canonical for versioning/parsing while generating a readable index and metrics for human retrieval/adoption.
applicability: File-based knowledge stores that need both machine reliability and human browsing.

title: Durable outbox with foreground-auth handoff
statement: Persist retryable state and recovery metadata without credentials, let background infrastructure signal pending work, and perform authenticated delivery in the foreground where session credentials already exist.
applicability: Local-first browser/PWA systems where session credentials are intentionally non-persistent but offline work still needs durable retry and conflict recovery.

title: Dry-run, approve, revalidate, apply, rollback selectively
statement: For brownfield canonicalization, classify without mutation, require explicit approval, re-check candidates at apply time, checkpoint first and reverse only affected entities while blocking rollback if later work depends on them.
applicability: Incremental migrations where legacy records remain operational while a canonical model is introduced and later user edits must not be lost by rollback.

title: Provider-safe preview entrypoint
statement: For a brownfield app that was local-only, add a dedicated hosted entrypoint that validates secrets before boot, binds provider PORT on 0.0.0.0, exposes a minimal unauthenticated healthcheck, routes persistent state to the provider volume and keeps production architecture boundaries explicit.
applicability: Local-first or desktop-served web apps being exposed temporarily through a managed HTTPS host before their final persistence/auth architecture is activated.

title: Context-aware deterministic decision contract
statement: Centralize deterministic decisions in one contract, make dependent context invalidation explicit, include relevant business context in cache keys, and exercise every alternate UI path through the same contract in regression tests.
applicability: Operational products where the same prioritization or recommended action is rendered through several UI surfaces and may be cached or enriched by AI.

title: Route minimal context by task
statement: Load a small core context plus the domain Skill/docs needed for the task instead of injecting the full project history into every agent invocation.
applicability: Any DUTRA agent task where excessive context increases cost, drift or contradictory instructions.

title: Bug to prevention to regression
statement: A material bug is not fully closed when behavior is patched; capture symptom and root cause, derive a prevention rule, attach a regression test and preserve provenance in the incident store.
applicability: Material bugs whose recurrence would cost data, user trust, deploy stability or commercial accuracy.

title: Stage-aware commercial guidance
statement: Select commercial objective, questions and next step from current relationship/pipeline context: gatekeeper seeks access, decision maker gets diagnosis, proposal gets blocker analysis, follow-up resumes commitments and customer/post-sale starts with experience.
applicability: Calls, messages, briefings and Next Best Action in the OG sales cycle.

title: Technical uncertainty becomes a validation state
statement: When technical evidence is insufficient or conflicting, preserve uncertainty as Precisa validar/Não determinada and route to manual validation rather than filling the gap from plausibility, code history or model inference.
applicability: OG vehicle/support/equalizer/PSI/application questions and generated quotes that depend on them.

title: Automation with manual escape
statement: Automation should accelerate common work while preserving review, edit, replace, add, remove, note and validate paths for real exceptions.
applicability: Technical quotes, CRM suggestions, proposals, follow-up planning and other workflows with legitimate account-specific exceptions.

title: Automation with manual escape
statement: Use automation to produce a strong default, then preserve edit, override, add, remove, observe and validate paths whenever real commercial/technical exceptions exist.
applicability: Quotes, technical application, orders, CRM suggestions and other operational flows where exceptional customer requirements are expected.

title: Metric numerator and denominator share one population
statement: Conversion metrics must derive numerator and denominator from compatible filters, attribution and time/population scope; historical totals cannot be divided by current-session denominators.
applicability: Funnels, list/session conversion, proposal and close-rate dashboards.

title: Skill to context to source routing
statement: Keep Skills procedural and compact, route each task to a bounded context set, and retain deeper evidence in canonical source files instead of copying the master context into every prompt.
applicability: Long-lived agent-assisted products where historical context must remain useful without being injected wholesale.

title: New shell over extracted brownfield engines
statement: When a new UX is approved but the legacy system owns mature domain logic, keep one user-facing shell and progressively extract/reuse legacy engines behind it until transitional bridges can be removed.
applicability: Brownfield UX migrations where reimplementation would discard tested business rules.

title: Mission prompts use minimal decision-changing context
statement: Execution prompts should reference bounded required context, conditional context and explicit do-not-load areas, scaling prompt depth with risk instead of copying the whole project history into each delegation.
applicability: Agent-assisted engineering/product work where long-lived project intelligence must guide execution without flooding context.

title: Prove shell independence and reconnect with real acknowledgement
statement: Block domain scripts to verify static shell/error recovery, inject renderer faults to prove other routes remain usable, traverse mobile/tablet/desktop sizes, and require real API acknowledgement after reconnect. When a browser emulator omits the network event, prove transport separately and label explicit event simulation; never mock sync success.
applicability: Responsive shell/startup/PWA changes in a mature local-first app; browser network event emulation must be distinguished from real transport and acknowledgement.

title: Concept first, code second for high-visual product work
statement: For high-visual work where user taste materially affects success, first translate screenshots, references, audio, sketches and reactions into a small design DNA and 2–3 concrete visual directions. Let the product owner select/refine a direction before spending implementation credits. Persist only the stable chosen principles; keep experiments cheap and reversible.
applicability: Proposal templates, dashboards, landing-like surfaces, brand moments and other DUTRA experiences where aesthetic direction and storytelling matter as much as functional correctness.
